insider_note: This substitution turns EVERY trig ratio in the integral into a rational function of t — that is the whole point of tan(x/2), and it is worth memorising the three replacement formulas cold rather than re-deriving them under exam pressure.

steps.label: Set up the tan(x/2) substitution
steps.why: Every rational function of sinx and cosx can be turned into a rational function of t through this one substitution, because sinx, cosx and dx all convert cleanly using the half-angle formulas.
common_mistakes: Misremembering cosx as (1+t²)/(1−t²) — the t² terms are the wrong way round.
Forgetting the 2 in dx = 2dt/(1+t²), which changes the final coefficient.
steps.memory_tip: sinx has 2t on top; cosx has (1−t²) on top — both share the same (1+t²) on the bottom.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify to a rational function of t
steps.why: The (1+t²) in the numerator and the (1+t²) hiding inside the denominator's fraction cancel completely — this cancellation is guaranteed to happen for every linear-in-sinx-and-cosx denominator.
common_mistakes: Not cancelling the (1+t²) factors, leaving a needlessly complicated rational function.
Sign slip when dividing 2 by −4t²+6t+4, which flips the whole fraction.
steps.memory_tip: The (1+t²) on top ALWAYS cancels one hiding in the bottom — look for it before doing anything else.

steps.label: Complete the square in t and apply the log formula
steps.why: The quadratic 2t²−3t−2 completes to a DIFFERENCE of squares, so this is a log-formula integral, exactly like any x²−a² denominator, just now in the variable t.
common_mistakes: Trying to apply the Tan⁻¹ formula here, which only applies to a SUM of squares.
Losing the leading −(1/2) factor picked up in the previous step.
steps.memory_tip: t²−a² in the completed square ⇒ log formula, the same rule that applies when the quadratic is in x.

steps.label: Back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: Clearing the internal fractions and writing t back as tan(x/2) returns the answer to the original variable x, which is what the question actually asked for.
common_mistakes: Leaving the final answer in terms of t instead of substituting tan(x/2) back in.
steps.memory_tip: The LAST move in every tan(x/2) integral is always the same: swap t back for tan(x/2).
